headline: January 2025's company-wide MoM revenue collapse is ordinary seasonality: December peaks and January troughs every year, budget assumed the same drop, and January 2025 was up 2.6% YoY.

evidence.what: Company net revenue Dec 2024 to Jan 2025, actual vs the same step in budget
evidence.figures: actual EUR 15.97M to EUR 11.38M (-28.7%); budget EUR 15.90M to EUR 11.57M (-27.2%) - the budget anticipated an equal drop

evidence.what: Jan 2025 year-on-year and vs budget
evidence.figures: EUR 11.38M vs Jan 2024 EUR 11.10M = +2.6% YoY; vs budget EUR 11.57M = -1.6%

evidence.what: Seasonal shape repeats both years: Nov to Dec jump then Dec to Jan fall

recommended_action: Read January against the prior January and budget, not against December; no action.

headline: The recurring Nordics (and company) material-cost flags are volume-driven, not input-cost inflation: material cost per unit is flat year-on-year and on or below budget.

evidence.what: Nordics material cost per unit, actual vs budget, through 2025
evidence.figures: actual approx EUR 1.27-1.33/unit vs budget approx EUR 1.29-1.32/unit; YoY change roughly -1% to -3% (flat to slightly down). Dec: EUR 1.271 actual vs EUR 1.288 budget

evidence.what: Nordics volume YoY vs material-cost euro YoY
evidence.figures: volume +10% to +20% each month; material-cost euros +8% to +17% YoY - the euro rise tracks volume, not price

evidence.what: Nordics material_cost price/volume/mix decomposition FY2025
evidence.figures: total +EUR 3.12M = volume +EUR 3.57M, mix -EUR 0.49M, price +EUR 0.05M; price effect near zero = no unit-cost inflation

recommended_action: Do not action the material-cost flag as a procurement or supplier problem; the euro increase is units sold.

headline: Behind the Nordics flags sits a real ~4pp gross-margin loss driven by a step-up in Home Care promotional discounting (6% to 19% of gross from February) and a volume shift into that low-margin line.
claimed_cause: From February 2025 Nordics roughly tripled promotional discount depth on Home Care (5.98% to 18.8% of gross), cutting Home Care net price EUR 2.50 to EUR 2.18/unit and its gross margin 27.6% to 16.5%, while Home Care's share of Nordics volume rose 36% to 46% - together pulling Nordics gross margin from ~43% to ~38-40%.

evidence.what: Nordics Home Care FY2024 vs FY2025: discount %, net price/unit, gross margin, volume share
evidence.figures: discount 5.98% to 18.84%; net/unit EUR 2.500 to EUR 2.184; gross margin 27.6% to 16.5%; volume share 36.3% to 45.5%

evidence.what: Nordics blended discount % and gross margin, Jan vs Feb 2025 onward
evidence.figures: discount 5.82% (Jan) steps to 10.16% (Feb) and holds ~9.6-10.3%; gross margin 42.3% (Jan) falls to ~38-40%

evidence.what: Nordics list price actual vs budget FY2025, all lines
evidence.figures: within -0.4% to -0.5% of budget - list prices were held; the gap is promotional discount, not list-price cuts

recommended_action: Review the Nordics Home Care promotional calendar and discount authority; test whether the extra volume covers the margin given away.

headline: Baltics & Poland's flagged revenue growth is genuine, broad-based volume (+30% to +46% YoY, every customer), not price - but it is unprofitable: EBITDA is below budget and down ~40% YoY.
claimed_cause: The volume-led growth is being bought: blended discount rose 8% to 17% of gross (gross margin 40.8% to 36.2%) and opex overran budget (S&M +23%, admin +22%), so although gross profit beat budget by EUR 1.44M, reported EBITDA is EUR 0.82M below budget and December EBITDA is -39.5% YoY.

evidence.what: B&P net revenue decomposition and customer spread
evidence.figures: total +EUR 8.39M = volume +EUR 10.18M, mix -EUR 0.14M, price -EUR 1.65M; every one of the 11 customers grew +21% or +30% - no single-customer concentration

evidence.what: B&P discount % and gross margin FY2024 to FY2025
evidence.figures: discount 8.1% to 17.1% across 2025; gross margin 40.8% (Jan) to 36.2% (Dec), -5.8pp YoY by December

evidence.what: B&P FY2025 opex and EBITDA vs budget
evidence.figures: S&M EUR 7.09M vs EUR 5.76M (+23%); admin EUR 5.09M vs EUR 4.16M (+22%); EBITDA EUR 2.95M vs budget EUR 3.77M

recommended_action: Decide whether B&P's ramp is a deliberate share-buy with a payback plan or margin leakage; do not read the revenue beat as good news without the EBITDA line beside it.

headline: The EBITDA-vs-budget miss is two different problems: Nordics is a EUR 4.23M gross-profit shortfall (discounting), Baltics & Poland is a EUR 2.26M opex overspend; Central Europe is broadly on plan.
claimed_cause: FY2025 EBITDA-vs-budget bridge by BU: Nordics -EUR 2.18M (gross profit -EUR 4.23M from margin loss, offset by the +EUR 2.2M April one-off other income); Baltics & Poland -EUR 0.82M (gross profit +EUR 1.44M but S&M -EUR 1.33M and admin -EUR 0.93M vs budget); Central Europe -EUR 0.44M (small gross-profit miss, opex on budget).

evidence.what: FY2025 reported EBITDA vs budget by BU
evidence.figures: Nordics EUR 9.24M vs 11.42M; B&P EUR 2.95M vs 3.77M; CE EUR 5.51M vs 5.95M

evidence.what: Component variances driving each BU miss
evidence.figures: Nordics: gross profit -EUR 4.23M, other income +EUR 2.20M; B&P: gross profit +EUR 1.44M, S&M -EUR 1.33M, admin -EUR 0.93M

recommended_action: Treat the two EBITDA drivers separately - Nordics promotional pricing and Baltics & Poland cost-to-grow - not as one 'EBITDA below budget' line.

headline: Central Europe's DSO deterioration (to 76.7 days, +23 YoY) is essentially one distributor: Rheinkauf Gruppe's receivable grew from 1.5 to 3.6 months of its sales while its revenue was flat, and it is 87% of the BU's receivables build.
claimed_cause: Rheinkauf Gruppe's monthly collections fell sharply from February 2025 (approx EUR 0.56-0.76M against ~EUR 1.15M of monthly revenue), so its closing receivable rose EUR 2.06M to EUR 4.49M - roughly 95-110 days of sales against 45-day terms. Its revenue rose only 4.4% YoY, so this is slower payment, not more sales.

evidence.what: Rheinkauf closing AR Dec 2024 vs Dec 2025 and its share of the CE build
evidence.figures: EUR 2.06M to EUR 4.49M (+EUR 2.43M) = 86.7% of CE's +EUR 2.81M receivables build; AR/monthly-revenue ratio 1.5 to ~3.4 (peaking 3.6)

evidence.what: Rheinkauf collections vs revenue through 2025
evidence.figures: collections EUR 0.56-1.01M/month against ~EUR 1.1-1.3M revenue for most of Feb-Nov; revenue FY2024 EUR 13.51M to FY2025 EUR 14.11M (+4.4%)

evidence.what: Terms vs implied DSO, Rheinkauf vs peers
evidence.figures: contractual 45 days; implied ~95-110 days by H2 2025; every other CE customer sits at 1.4-2.3 months of sales

recommended_action: Put Rheinkauf Gruppe's ~EUR 4.5M balance (about EUR 2.4M beyond a normal 45-day level) on the agenda as a collection and credit-limit matter.

headline: April's +196% EBITDA spike is a single EUR 2.2M one-off other-income entry booked to Nordics, alongside a EUR 5.5M investing cash inflow the same month; underlying EBITDA that month was EUR 1.19M, in line with the run-rate.

evidence.what: Other income by month and BU
evidence.figures: EUR 2,200,000 in April 2025, Nordics; zero in every other month and BU across all 24 months

evidence.what: Investing cash flow across the dataset
evidence.figures: EUR 5,500,000 in April 2025 - the only non-zero investing line in 24 months, consistent with a one-off asset disposal

evidence.what: Reported vs underlying EBITDA, April 2025
evidence.figures: reported EUR 3.39M (25.1% of net revenue) vs underlying EUR 1.19M (8.8%) - the spike is entirely the one-off

recommended_action: Exclude the EUR 2.2M from run-rate and trend comparisons; it is non-operational.

headline: Stripping the EUR 2.2M one-off, underlying EBITDA fell 13.7% YoY (EUR 17.96M to EUR 15.50M) even as revenue rose 8.6% - reported EBITDA looks roughly flat only because of that one-off.
claimed_cause: Revenue grew EUR 154.7M to EUR 168.0M (+8.6%) but gross margin fell 42.5% to 40.2% and underlying EBITDA margin 11.6% to 9.2%; the EUR 2.2M April other income lifts reported FY EBITDA to EUR 17.70M (-1.4% YoY), disguising the underlying decline.

evidence.what: FY2024 vs FY2025 company revenue, gross margin, reported and underlying EBITDA
evidence.figures: net revenue EUR 154.68M to 168.03M (+8.6%); gross margin 42.5% to 40.2%; reported EBITDA EUR 17.96M to 17.70M (-1.4%); underlying (ex other income) EUR 17.96M to 15.50M (-13.7%)

recommended_action: Present underlying EBITDA (ex the EUR 2.2M) as the headline; the year is 'grew the top line, lost profit', not 'flat'.

headline: The margin erosion is a promotional-discount step-change (gross-to-net discount 5.8% to 10.4% of gross from February 2025), not a cost problem - but the pack has no discount/price measure, so it surfaces only as 'material cost'.
claimed_cause: Company promotional discounts stepped from ~5.8% of gross (all of 2024 and Jan 2025) to 8.4% in February and 10.4% by December, concentrated in Nordics Home Care and across all Baltics & Poland lines; unit material cost is flat and on budget everywhere, so the recurring material-cost flags point the board at suppliers when the lever is promotional pricing.

evidence.what: Company gross-to-net discount % by month
evidence.figures: 5.73-6.18% throughout 2024 and Jan 2025; 8.43% in Feb 2025 rising to 10.43% by Dec 2025

evidence.what: Company net-revenue price and mix effects vs material-cost price effect FY2025
evidence.figures: net revenue price -EUR 2.98M and mix -EUR 5.91M; material-cost price +EUR 0.03M - the erosion is on the revenue/discount side

evidence.what: Material cost per unit vs budget, all three BUs
evidence.figures: within ~1% of budget in every BU - no input-cost inflation anywhere

recommended_action: Add a discount / net-price-realisation measure to the pack and manage promotions directly; the material-cost flags are not procurement issues.

headline: Operating cash flow (EUR 10.3M FY2025) ran well below underlying EBITDA (EUR 15.5M) as receivables grew EUR 3.9M; the EUR 15.8M rise in the cash balance is flattered by the EUR 5.5M one-off investing inflow.
claimed_cause: FY2025 operating cash flow was EUR 10.3M against underlying EBITDA of EUR 15.5M; company receivables rose EUR 17.67M to EUR 21.53M (+EUR 3.86M), the single largest piece being Rheinkauf. The cash balance rose EUR 21.69M to EUR 37.49M, of which EUR 5.5M is the April investing inflow - so recurring operating cash generation is modest.

evidence.what: FY2025 operating and investing cash flow and the cash bridge
evidence.figures: operating CF EUR 10.30M; investing CF EUR 5.50M; cash closing EUR 21.69M (Dec 2024) to EUR 37.49M (Dec 2025)

evidence.what: Company receivables Dec 2024 vs Dec 2025
evidence.figures: EUR 17.67M to EUR 21.53M, a EUR 3.86M drag on operating cash

recommended_action: Read the cash build with the one-off and receivables movement stripped out; collecting the Central Europe balance would release roughly EUR 2-2.5M.
